title: Anthropic is hiring fewer juniors, says AI now does 6 times more work than humans
source_used: Anthropic research page 'How employment is changing at Anthropic' (full text) and India Today (full text)
key_facts: The proportion of junior technical hires at Anthropic fell from 27% to 9%; the share of junior-level employees in technical departments slipped from 21% to 14% since early 2025.
The technical departments' share of Anthropic's employment fell from 61% to 56% over the last year, partly because sales, finance and recruiting hiring grew faster.
By August, the AI agents run by employees worked about six times as many hours as their human handlers; in March 2026 combined autonomous and interactive agent hours first passed human work hours.

Researchers followed 192 engineers who adopted coding agents against 74 who did not; output rose after adoption and agent-written code was removed or reverted at about the same rate as human-written code.

Employees at the company for at least a year were 50% more likely to move across departments each month in 2026 than in 2025; Anthropic set up an early warning system for jobs at risk and prioritises internal moves.
Claude sessions spend about 80% of their time waiting for human input, and reading the output would take more than half a work week even for non-technical teams.
The study uses internal data and 17 employee interviews; one account executive said Claude automations replaced about 20% of prior tasks and let them talk to 30% more customers.
quote_evidence: The proportion of junior technical hires fell even faster, from 27% to 9%.
By August interactive AI agent hours outnumbered employees' 6 to 1.
One engineer described work as facing "an army of Claudes, with every one asking for my attention."
why_it_matters_hint: A leading AI lab's own data show fewer junior technical hires as agents take on more work.
notes: Company's own research about itself; no outside review reported.
